FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio are chasing history as they journey north to face a Torino side whose form has nosedived in recent weeks.

Match News and Current Form

A purple patch of three successive wins in October must now feel like a distant memory for Torino, who’ve picked up just one point in four outings since. Sat on 14 points after 12 games for a third successive Serie A season, Torino’s current slump appears unlikely to end here given they’ve picked up just one point this term against teams currently in the top half (D1, L5), losing all three home fixtures therein. Confidence is unlikely to be drawn from a return home either, as Ignazio Abate’s men have won just twice here this season (D1, L3), and are enduring their longest-ever run without a home clean sheet in Serie A (11 games).

The runaway Lazio train shows no sign of slowing down, with last week’s 3-0 win over Lecce cementing their two-point lead at the Serie A summit and keeping them on course for a first Scudetto since 2000. Another win here would take the Biancocelesti to 35 points after 13 games, and given that only one side has ever previously failed to win the title from that position without having points deducted, confidence must be growing of a fairytale story coming true. Manager Gennaro Gattuso will need just a third managerial win over Torino to take his side there (D3, L2), but would likely settle for keeping Lazio unbeaten in their first seven away matches of a Serie A season for just the third time ever.

Head-to-Head History

Torino were winless in five H2Hs (D2, L3) before winning last season’s corresponding fixture 2-0 in March, giving them the chance to post back-to-back Serie A wins against Lazio for the first time since 2013.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Torino have conceded 14 of their 18 Serie A goals this term after half-time.

None of Torino’s last eight competitive home games featured over 2.5 yellow cards.

Lazio went on to win both Serie A games they conceded first in this season.

Lazio failed to score in each of their last nine away league defeats.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Torino’s Giovanni Simeone must relish this fixture having scored a career-high 11 times against Lazio, at least five more than any other opponent, but he’s only ever managed two wins against them (D5, L12). A brace last weekend took Tijjani Noslin to six goal involvements in his last four matches (G4, A2), and he could become the first Lazio player since Ciro Immobile in October 2021 to directly contribute to a goal in five straight Serie A games here.

Torino lost Rafik Belghali and Ardian Ismajli to injury last week, while Lazio were without Josip Šutalo, Nuno Tavares and Mattia Zaccagni against Lecce.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given that Torino tend to keep things tight early, a half-time draw and Lazio win looks a good option here.

Author: Ryan Fisher
